4.3.1.5.3 Concepts of data access
Tables 4.9 and 4.10 summarize the characteristics of implicit versus explicit data re-
ception and transmission.
Implicit Read
Explicit Read
Receiving of data element values is
performed only once when runnable
starts
Runnable decides when and how often
a data element value is received
Values of data elements do not change
while runnable is running.
Runnable can always decide to receive
the latest value
Several API calls to the same signal
always yield the same data element
value
Several API calls to the same signal
may yield different data element values
Runnable must terminate (all cate-
gories)
Runnable is of cat. 1B or 2
Table 4.9: Implicit vs. explicit read
Implicit Write
Explicit Write
Sending of data element values is only
done once after runnable returns
Runnable can decide when sending of
data element values is done via the
API call
Several usages of the API call inside
the runnable cause only one data ele-
ment transmission
Several usages of the API call inside
the runnable cause several transmis-
sions of the data element content. (De-
pending on the behavior of COM, the
number of API calls and the number
of transmissions are not necessarily
equal.)
Runnable must terminate (all cate-
gories)
Runnable is cat. 1B or 2
Table 4.10: Implicit vs. explicit write
